svg.title: Fig. 184 — The loxodrome on the sphere and its stereographic image, an equiangular spiral
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 184, page 207. Section: spirals.

g.data-text: The sphere with its meridians, the north pole N at the top and the south pole S at the bottom (the double circle: the centre of projection), and the plane through the equator.

The loxodrome: the curve that cuts every meridian at the same angle (the course of a ship holding a fixed compass heading). From the equator it winds round the sphere, climbing toward the pole N, which it approaches but never reaches.
The stereographic projection from S: the straight line from S through a point Q of the loxodrome meets the plane of the equator at the point q. Do this for several points.
The images q fill the equiangular spiral about the centre of the plane: the stereographic image of a loxodrome. Where the loxodrome meets the equator, its image meets the equator circle of the plane.
